notes.meaning: Paul gives Timothy a most serious charge in the presence of God and Jesus Christ. Jesus is coming again in royal glory to judge all people, both those still alive and those who have died. Remembering that every worker must give an account to the Lord should urge us to stay faithful.

differ.view: Gill understands Christ's kingdom here as a literal thousand-year reign on earth, judging believers at the beginning and the wicked at the end.
Ellicott sees the kingdom as Christ's everlasting reign without end, which later became part of the early church creeds.

notes.meaning: Timothy is commanded to preach God's message like a royal messenger announcing a king. He must be ready to do this at all times, whether the situation is convenient or dangerous. His teaching must patiently correct wrong ideas, warn against sin, and comfort believers.

A day is coming when churchgoers will no longer put up with healthy Bible teaching that exposes their sins. Instead, they will gather crowds of teachers who flatter them and say only what their sinful desires want to hear. Their ears itch for novelty rather than the plain truth.

People who shut their ears to God's truth will wander off into foolish myths and made-up stories. Because they reject what is right, God justly lets them be misled by empty teaching. Those who refuse the light quickly end up trapped in darkness.

Timothy must keep a cool head, stay alert, and willingly endure any suffering that comes his way. He is told to do the work of an evangelist, which means a person who spreads the good news of Jesus. By fulfilling all his duties, he will give clear proof that he is a genuine servant of God.

Paul realizes that his life is about to end, comparing his death to wine poured out as an offering to God. He pictures dying like a ship untying its ropes to leave the harbor. For the believer, death is not destruction, but a departure into the presence of Christ.

Paul looks back on his life as an athletic contest run for Christ. He fought hard in the noble struggle against sin, and he crossed the finish line of the race set before him. Above all, he guarded the true gospel and remained completely loyal to his Master.

Paul looks forward to the crown of righteousness that awaits him in heaven. The Lord Jesus is the fair Judge who awards this victor's prize, unlike the Roman court that condemned Paul. This wonderful reward is promised not only to apostles, but to all who eagerly look forward to Christ's return.

differ.view: Calvin and Watson argue that believers can never earn this crown through their own works, since it is a free gift based entirely on Christ's righteousness given through faith.
Clarke explains that a believer can claim this crown as a promised reward that God graciously gives in return for faithful service.

notes.meaning: Paul asks Timothy to do everything he can to come visit him soon. The apostle was sitting in a lonely prison cell and wanted the comfort of his dear companion before his execution. Even strong leaders need the warm presence of trusted Christian friends.

Paul grieves that his former coworker Demas had abandoned him because he loved the ease and safety of this present world. Other companions had departed on ministry trips, with Crescens going to Galatia and Titus to Dalmatia. Worldly comfort often pulls people away from standing with suffering Christians.

Only Luke remained with Paul in Rome to assist him in prison. Paul tells Timothy to find Mark and bring him along, because Mark had proved very useful for the work of the gospel. Though Paul had once refused to travel with Mark after an early failure, he was now glad to welcome him back.

Paul notes that he had sent his coworker Tychicus away on a mission to Ephesus. This dependable brother could help lead the church there while Timothy traveled to Rome. Paul made sure the churches were cared for even while his own life hung in the balance.

Paul asks Timothy to pick up the heavy traveling coat he had left with Carpus in Troas. He also urgently requests his book rolls and the animal skins used for writing. Even in a cold dungeon on the brink of death, Paul still wanted to study, write, and stay warm.

Paul warns about a metal craftsman named Alexander who had done great damage to his work. Instead of seeking personal revenge, Paul leaves the man to the justice of God, who will repay everyone fairly for what they have done. We can leave wrongdoers safely in God's hands.

Timothy must watch out for Alexander because this man fiercely fought against the gospel message. His attacks were directed against God's truth, not just Paul personally. Christians must be on guard against those who actively try to tear down the faith.

At his first court appearance in Rome, not one fellow Christian stood up to speak for Paul, and everyone deserted him out of fear. Rather than becoming bitter, Paul prayed that God would forgive them for their weakness. Showing mercy to friends who fail us is the true way of Jesus.

Even though human friends ran away, the Lord Jesus stood right beside Paul and filled him with power. This courage allowed Paul to proclaim the good news boldly so that the Gentile rulers and court listeners could hear it. God delivered him from immediate execution, which Paul compares to escaping the jaws of a lion.

Paul was confident that the Lord would protect him from every evil trap and keep him from denying his faith. Even if his earthly life was taken, God would carry him safely into His heavenly kingdom. Thinking of God's perfect rescue causes Paul to erupt in praise and give Him glory forever.

Paul sends warm greetings to his longtime friends Prisca and Aquila, who had served Christ alongside him for years. He also sends love to the family of Onesiphorus, who had searched out Paul and helped him in prison. Even in his darkest moments, Paul kept thinking of other believers.

Paul gives updates about two other coworkers, noting that Erastus stayed at Corinth and Trophimus was left sick at Miletus. Although God gave the apostles power to heal diseases for special signs, they could not heal people whenever they wanted. Sickness is not always caused by sin, and healing remains in God's hands.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern groups teach that God always promises physical healing if a believer has enough faith, but commentators point out that Paul leaving a faithful friend sick shows healing is never guaranteed or controlled by human will.

notes.meaning: Paul urges Timothy once more to hurry and arrive before winter. Sea travel was shut down by dangerous winter storms, and Paul would need his warm coat and friends as the weather worsened. He passes along greetings from several Roman Christians, showing that a community of faith still surrounded him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching identifies the Linus mentioned in this verse as the man who succeeded Peter as the second bishop of Rome.

notes.meaning: Paul ends his final letter with a blessing, praying that the Lord Jesus will be close to Timothy's spirit. He also prays for God's grace, which means His undeserved love and favor, to rest on the entire church. Having Christ's presence and grace is everything believers need to endure until the end.
